description.value: The study examined whether pretreatment fMRI cue reactivity predicts differential relapse response to naltrexone versus acamprosate in alcohol-dependent patients.

value: We hypothesized that the group of patients who had higher levels of alcohol-associated pretreatment cue reactivity in reward-related areas such as the VS would respond better to naltrexone than the group with low or no cue reactivity.
Conversely, acamprosate is not believed to influence the positive reinforcement effects of alcohol, but to modulate brain glutamate levels.
For this reason, we did not expect high cue reactivity in the VS to predict positive outcomes in patients randomized to acamprosate.
